title: Optimal single-copy estimation of quantum state moments: why $\operatorname{Tr}(ρ^3)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(ρ^4)$ are equally hard
summary: Estimating nonlinear properties of an unknown quantum state with restrictive experimental accessibility is a fundamental problem in quantum learning. We study the sample complexity of estimating the state moments $\operatorname{Tr}(ρ^t)$, allowing arbitrary adaptive single-copy measurements. While purity estimation has optimal sample complexity $Θ(\sqrt d)$ at constant additive error, the optimal dimension dependence for higher moments has remained unclear.
